newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip despite cement, mills trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip despite cement, mills trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped two points on Monday despite a good showing from cement firms and mills, brokers said.
"The market is still sleepy," said Youssef Khalil of Delta/EAB. "It may take some time to pick up again."
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed at 386.98 from 388.98 on Sunday while turnover was an unsually high 142.34 million pounds ($41.93 million).
The sale of 300,000 shares in the state-owned Alexandria Commerical and Maritime Bank accounted for more than 90 million pounds of the day's total volume.
The state initially offered investors 20,400 shares or 1.8 percent of the joint venture bank. The bank's rarely-traded shares are listed in U.S. dollars and Egyptian pounds.
Brokers and the CMA said the shares were sold at 301 pounds each. Bidding started at 140 pounds per share.
Broker Mohammed Abdullah of Intercapital told Reuters he believed bidding got out of hand for the shares on offer.

"The closing price of 301 pounds is ridiculously high. We had joined the bidding but pulled out when it went above 201. Investors are not that sophisticated and they thought it was a better deal than it actually is," Abdullah said.
He said cement shares and milling shares did well because of attractive prices and a reputation for being solid.
"Cement shares are the most liquid and stable on the market, and mills are second best in terms of liquidity but maybe not stability because they can be volatile," Abdullah said.
Helwan Portland Cement was the day's most active share, closing one pound higher at 80 after trade in more than 6.60 million pounds.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement also did well, with shares worth more than 4.10 million pounds changing hands but it closed slightly higher at 97.04 pounds.

North Cairo Flour Mills topped the mills, closing one pound higher at 192 after trading in more than four million pounds. Southern Cairo Flour Mills closed 0.75 pounds higher at 80.01 while Central Egypt Flour Mills closed 0.25 pounds higher at 55.25.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 598.17 points from 608.22 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 267.78 from 267.29 points.
Out of the 78 shares traded, 32 gained, 31 lost and 15 ended unchanged.
